::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_27 — OrgPath and Identity Governance
:::


::: {.callout-note}
Identity governance was never a clean discipline in the AD era — it was a set of informal dependencies baked into a directory that nobody audited until they had to migrate away from it. This book excavates those dependencies, names what broke when AD left, and shows how UIAO replaces each one with something observable: a JML pipeline that fires on HRIT diffs, an OrgPath-addressed routing layer that answers "who approves this," a FedRAMP-Moderate non-employee warehouse in SailPoint NERM, and a service identity orphan detector that catches what every previous governance model missed. The governance gap AD leaves behind is real; the pipeline that fills it is now running.
:::

## Companion canon

For the normative specifications this narrative paraphrases:

- [ADR-059 — SailPoint NERM Boundary Exception](/docs/adr/adr-059-sailpoint-adapter-family.html) — the carve-out that adds SailPoint NERM as UIAO's second Commercial exception and the `sailpoint-nerm` conformance adapter slot.
- [ADR-092 — Active Governance](/docs/adr/adr-092-active-governance.html) — the control-plane/data-plane boundary, provider-incorporation contract, and L0–L4 actuation ladder that govern how the JML pipeline is positioned.
- [UIAO_141 — Customer Identity Model](/customer-documents/reference-architecture/codebook.html) — the non-employee Customer Identity Record (CIR) target that NERM is the operational substrate for.
- [UIAO_142 — Customer KYC Onboarding & Reciprocity Runbook](/customer-documents/reference-architecture/codebook.html) — the onboarding contract and reciprocal-consumption entitlement doctrine.
- [OrgPath Codebook](/customer-documents/reference-architecture/codebook.html) — the fifteen-facet Model C schema that drives approval routing and entitlement scoping throughout this book.
- [Architecture Decision Records](/docs/adr/index.html) — the binding record; this book is governed primarily by ADR-059, ADR-092, ADRs 051–056, and UIAO_141/142/200.
